items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: so I made an appointment with Lee Konitz it was just a trio: Lee, Sonny Dallas and myself

ctx.x: So you were making some records at this point do you remember any of the recordings that you made at this point?
so I made an appointment with Lee Konitz it was just a trio: Lee, Sonny Dallas and myself at a studio on 7th Avenue or something. It wasn’t one of the regular studios. We just started playing.
So this is pretty interesting, you’re playing in a piano-less trio?

items.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember that there was a date with Elvin and Sonny. I had asked Max [Roach] to do it and he’s said he couldn’t do it and he suggested Elvin.

ctx.x: I remember that there was a date with Elvin and Sonny. I had asked Max [Roach] to do it and he’s said he couldn’t do it and he suggested Elvin. That’s the way it started. Then I wanted to do another day with Elvin and he was traveling so I asked Nick.
That’s very curious because there’s much more stuff with Nick. There’s about, oh god, fifteen to twenty titles with Nick from two days of recording.
